headline: Asia: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Asia: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
- South Asia: 4 FBR officials, traffic policeman martyred in DI Khan attacks: police.
- Western Russia: Ukraine presented drone that automatically detects and attacks Russian electronic warfare systems.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
Following the Industrial Disputes Tribunal’s landmark ruling in favour of doctors in their long-running allowances dispute with the State, senior trade unionist Lambert Brown says the medical practitioners are ready to meet with the Government to implement the award. In a quick response on Monday, Brown said the doctors were pleased with the outcome. “We receive the award [ruling] just after 4 p.m. and we can confirm that award is in favour of the doctors and the two issues before the tribunal,” he said.
United States: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match.
- Buenos Aires Herald, just now: Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match.
The Argentine football superstar called the distinction ‘an honor,’ adding that it was awarded to him on a ‘very special day’ La entrada Lionel Messi receives UBA honorary doctorate before final national team match se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukraine presented drone that automatically detects and attacks Russian electronic warfare systems.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Ukraine presented drone that automatically detects and attacks Russian electronic warfare systems.
A Ukrainian strike UAV capable of automatically detecting radio emission sources and homing in on them has appeared on the Brave1 Market.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Man killed in strike on warehouse in Zaporizhzhia.
A 47-year-old man has been killed and several injured as a result of a Russian strike on a warehouse in the city of Zaporizhzhia on 6 October.
- The Moscow Times, 9 hours ago: Kremlin Warns Lithuania Lifting Nuclear Arms Ban Risks Escalation.
The move comes on the heels of Estonia announcing it was moving its troops closer to the country's border with Russia.
- The Moscow Times, 5 hours ago: Russia Drops Criminal Case Against Children’s Hospice Founder Lida Moniava.
Moniava had been charged with spreading “false information” about Russia’s army for a post about Ukrainian civilians killed in Russian attacks.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
- Balkan Insight, 9 hours ago: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
Lawyers for one of 14 people targeted by Pegasus spyware file criminal complaint against Serbian intelligence agency officials, police and the Israeli company behind the surveillance technology after institutions fail to react.
- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Kosovo Protesters Against Hague Court Gather Again After Clashes.
After violent clashes on Monday night, protesters started to reassemble in Pristina to demand legal changes to curb the powers of the Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court following convictions of guerrilla leaders.
- Balkan Insight, 3 hours ago: Kosovo Political Leaders Trade Blame as Another Election Looms.
New election likely as political parties fail to agree on electing a president and protesters keep up pressure for adoption of law curbing powers of Kosovo Specialist Chambers, following its conviction of wartime guerrilla leaders.
- Balkan Insight, 14 hours ago: From Streets to Polling Stations: Serbia’s Student Movement Takes Electoral Test.
Nearly two years after it was created, Serbia’s student movement is contesting a national election – but experts warn that winning power would only be the start of the challenge.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Tuareg rebels withdraw from strategic town of Kidal in northern Mali.
The Azawad Liberation Front said sustained air strikes by Malian troops and Russian allies forced its tactical retreat.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Three years after October 7, is the IDF ready to stop another invasion? - analysis.
Three years after October 7, the IDF has more troops, intelligence capabilities, and warning systems, but questions remain over whether Israel could again be caught by surprise.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Russia preparing 'massive attack' against Ukraine, Zelensky warns as he urges partner support.
"There is updated intelligence indicating that Russia is preparing a massive attack," Zelensky said in his nightly video address.

- Africanews, 23 hours ago: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
Following almost two weeks of internal conflict that threatens a wider regional war in Ethiopia, the country's prime minister has vowed that government forces are ready to bring a rebel offensive under control.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Tigray violence drives risk of Ethiopia-Eritrea war, analyst says.
Renewed fighting between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan rebels increases risks of an escalation into a wider regional conflict, according to International Crisis Group analyst Magnus Taylor.
- Africanews, 5 hours ago: Renewed violence in Ethiopia's Tigray leaves dozens of children wounded.
Children are among the dozens of civilians killed or injured in Tigray since fighting broke out between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan rebels in September.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 5 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Tungwarara Confirms He Was Airlifted, Refutes Claims He Is Sick - Sources Say He Is Now Recovering.

ASIA
Asia - bottom line: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
- South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
Iran and Saudi Arabia are edging dangerously closer to direct conflict, analysts warn, after Riyadh resumed major air strikes on Yemen’s Tehran-allied Houthi rebels this week, ending a four-year lull. More than 100 Saudi warplanes bombed rebel positions on Monday, enabling Yemeni government forces to retake much of the Red Sea coastal territory the Houthis seized last month. The Houthis had been aided by embedded Iranian military advisers. Analysts expect the Houthis to retaliate by intensifying...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Moscow Times, 12 hours ago: Ukraine attacks Moscow region with 650 drones as both sides step up strikes.
A massive attack involving 650 drones targeted Moscow overnight, leaving at least two dead, Russian authorities said on Tuesday. Most of the drones were destroyed by air defences at long range, including 105 intercepted as they approached the capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on Telegram. Russian state news agency Tass reported it was the second-largest drone attack on the capital region in the past two years. The dead included a 71-year-old man pulled from under the rubble ‌of a house...
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: UK police arrest seventh man linked to security incident at US-run airbase.
British police on Tuesday arrested a 22-year-old man in London on suspicion of a terror offence over a security incident at a US-run military airbase in England that authorities have linked to Iran. The arrest is the seventh in connection with a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, located 160km (100 miles) west of London, which has been used by American bombers to strike Iran during this year’s war. Five British men in their 20s were detained near the perimeter of the base in the early hours of...
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: Why India is getting serious about ending the Ukraine war.
India’s recent push to become more involved in helping end the Russia-Ukraine war comes as the costs of the conflict continue to mount for New Delhi, amid the threat of US tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy and a recent drone attack on an Indian-owned pharmaceutical plant in Ukraine. Sunday morning’s drone attack destroyed a large part of Kusum Group’s factory in Sumy, killing one person and injuring several others. The company, which has manufactured generic medicines in Ukraine since...
South Asia - bottom line: 4 FBR officials, traffic policeman martyred in DI Khan attacks: police.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 4 FBR officials, traffic policeman martyred in DI Khan attacks: police.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Four Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials were martyred in firing by unidentified assailants near Qureshi Mor in Dera Ismail Khan, while a separate attack on a highway traffic police mobile near the Mufti Mahmood Chowk bypass left a constable martyred and another injured, police said on Tuesday. Dera Ismail Khan District Police Officer Ziauddin Ahmad told Dawn that two of the four FBR officials were serving with the board on a contractual basis. The assailants fled after the attacks, prompting police to cordon off the areas and launch search operations, the police added.
- The Hindu - International, 12 hours ago: Yemen, Saudi Arabia strike Houthis as counteroffensive gets underway.
The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Security forces kill 5 terrorists in North Waziristan IBO: state media.
Security forces on Tuesday killed five terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported. Two terrorists were injured in the operation, it said. Forces targeted hideouts of the terrorists, who belonged to Fitna al-Khawarij, according to security sources. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday commended the security forces for the successful IBO.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Dar warns of 'serious implications' for regional peace, security if Pakistan deprived of water share under IWT.
Attempts to deprive Pakistan of its rightful share of water would have “serious implications” for regional peace and security, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Tuesday, in an address regarding the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). The deputy premier was addressing the International Water Symposium convened by the Embassy of Pakistan in Austria in collaboration with the Diplomatic Academy of Vienna, according to the Foreign Office.
India - bottom line: In Dehradun Triple Murder, Couple And House Help Killed With Screwdriver.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: In Dehradun Triple Murder, Couple And House Help Killed With Screwdriver.
The victims have been identified as 80-year-old K S Kapoor, his 76-year-old wife Rajni Kapoor, and their 55-year-old domestic help, Tiliya Devi, who belonged to Darbhanga in Bihar.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base.
Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius has declared his willingness to finance the establishment of a permanent US military base in Lithuania. Since 2019, Lithuania has been hosting a rotating US battalion and is eager for a long-term military presence. Concurrently, the Lithuanian parliament is considering lifting constitutional prohibitions on nuclear weapons, a move that has drawn sharp criticism from Russia, citing heightened regional tensions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Astronomers find ‘phoenix planet’ born from ashes of a dying star.
A team of astronomers has discovered a second-generation planet orbiting a white dwarf named HS 0209+0832. This planet formed from the material that the white dwarf expelled during its death. The atmosphere of the white dwarf contains heavy elements such as zinc, copper, and niobium. This discovery could change the way astronomers search for similar planets around dead stars.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Rajnath Singh Launches First India-Made Fleet Support Ship In Vizag.
When these 43,500-tonne vessels enter service, they will refuel and resupply warships at sea, letting the Navy stay out longer and range farther across the Indian Ocean Region.

Australia - bottom line: Third driveway car firebombing in Melbourne in as many days.

Two cars have been destroyed and a home damaged by fire in another overnight arson attack in Melbourne.
- The Guardian - Australia, 17 hours ago: Angus Taylor vows biggest cut to migration in Australia’s history, slashing 650,000 temporary visas.
Opposition leader says Coalition would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor says a Coalition government would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years, calling the plan “the biggest cut to immigration in the history” of Australia. Following moves by One Nation and Labor to capitalise on growing anti-migration sentiment, the opposition leader announced plans by the Liberals and Nationals on Tuesday, promising net overseas migration rates of 130,000 in the third year and 160,000 in the fourth.

The Matildas will return to Victoria this year, with Geelong picked to host the second leg of a two-match series against Colombia
